=== ONE OBSERVATION, EXPLICITLY NOT CHARGED TO THIS PR ===

`RuleMode` is a `(str, Enum)` and every mode comparison in core/ uses `is`, including engine.py's two and this PR's two. `RuleConfig` is a frozen dataclass with no coercion in __init__, so `RuleConfig(mode="deny")` is constructible and, measured: `"deny" == RuleMode.DENY` is True while `"deny" is RuleMode.DENY` is False, and the fail-closed branch then silently does not fire. This is a real fail-open edge, but it is a PRE-EXISTING repo-wide convention (engine.py:69, 97, 100 predate this PR) and the only sanctioned construction path, load_policy_dict, goes through RuleMode.coerce and yields real enum members. #51 follows the house style rather than introducing the issue. Charging it here would be charging an innocent PR for main's convention. Raised for the owner; not a finding against #51.
